newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale/Dassault must speed up merge - minister.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale/Dassault must speed up merge - minister.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra called on Tuesday for a speeding up of the merger between French aircraft makers Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale in the light of the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas link up.
The U.S. merger shows "the need to accelerate the merger process between two remarkable aircraft builders in France, Dassault and Aerospatiale," he told parliament.
"I believe this (U.S.) merger is simply the desire clearly shown by the United States to have a dominant position in a strategically important industrial sector," he said.
"Europe must take up the challenge," he said.

Borotra pointed up the difference in scale between a merged Aerospatiale/Dassault, which would have annual turnover of 60 billion francs, compared to the new Boeing/McDonnell company which would have 250 billion.
The U.S. move also shows the "need to accelerate the evolution of the Airbus consortium to a company with its own equity to face up to the international challenge," he said.
Airbus particularly needs to push ahead with its planned A3XX large plane to seat 550 and the 100-seater to be built with China and Singapore, he said.
"Europe needs to realise the need to put in place an industrial strategy at the European level...This is the only way to face up to the challenge with which the Americans confront us," he added.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas announced on Sunday they planned to merge through a $13.3 billion stock swap to create the world's biggest aerospace company with annual turnover of $48 billion.
